title: The Citrus Docks
story:
The morning sun rose over the bustling riverfront of San Antonio del Río, casting golden light across stacked wooden crates and weathered timber pilings. James and Nico emerged from the damp shelter of the countryside paths onto the lively edge of the river docks, where the air hummed with the steady drone of motorized watercraft and carried the sharp, sweet scent of crushed citrus. Cargo boats bobbed against the muddy banks, and dockworkers called out to one another in the warm highland air.

Near a towering stack of wooden fruit boxes, an elderly dock worker struggled to corral a cascade of golden oranges that had spilled across the wooden decking. Remembering the careful wood-sanding routines he practiced in Aldea San Gabriel with Don Tadeo, James stepped forward without hesitation. With quick, sure movements, he gathered the rolling spheres together, gently placing them back into the slatted crate.

The old worker paused, wiping sweat from his brow, and looked down in surprise at his small, helpful companion. Breaking into a warm, weathered smile, he reached into an open crate and tossed James a couple of fresh, segmented orange slices. Nico, peering cautiously out from behind a thick hemp mooring rope with his large ears twitching, scurried forward to share the sweet reward, their recent tensions along the canal completely washed away by the bright morning.

With their bellies full of sweet citrus and their spirits lifted by the active rhythm of the wharf, James pulled out his polished brass pocket compass. He checked the needle against the southward-flowing river, mapping their new surroundings in his mind as the vibrant trade hub of San Antonio del Río opened up before them.
location: Riverside docks of San Antonio del Río
